hypothesis:
M0 on corpus v2: reproducing the M0 experiment against the v2 candidate corpus, which differs from v1 in exactly one decisive respect — it contains tool-call supervision.
Measured on identical raw input at the training boundary, the corrected Glaive adapter takes that source from 48,757 trainable records carrying zero tool calls to 97,475 carrying 48,726. Across the whole corpus the number of supervised records whose target contains a `<tool_call>` moves from 9 of 55,719 (0.0162%) in v1 to roughly half of everything trainable.
This is the test of the root cause. Both M0 and M1 failed the same way on v1 — call_f1 fell monotonically while over-calling vanished — and the claim was that the cause is the absence of a behaviour from the training signal rather than the training procedure. If that claim is right, the same procedure on v2 behaves differently.
The corpus is a partial rebuild: xlam and button are gated upstream and looptool's source was not located, so v2 is three sources of six and is not a drop-in replacement for v1. v1 is untouched and B0 remains pinned to it.
